cards.front: Recall a key point about Offences Against the Person
cards.back: Assault is causing the victim to fear immediate unlawful force — no physical contact is required

cards.front: Recall a key point about Offences Against the Person
cards.back: Battery is the unlawful application of force to another person — any unwanted touching can amount to battery

cards.front: Recall a key point about Offences Against the Person
cards.back: Assault and battery are summary offences tried in the Magistrates' Court, carrying up to 6 months' imprisonment

cards.front: Recall a key point about Offences Against the Person
cards.back: Section 47 OAPA 1861: actual bodily harm (ABH) — injury that is more than transient, including psychological harm

cards.front: Recall a key point about Offences Against the Person
cards.back: Section 20 OAPA 1861: wounding or grievous bodily harm (GBH) with malice aforethought — a break in both layers of skin

cards.front: Recall a key point about Offences Against the Person
cards.back: Section 18 OAPA 1861: wounding or GBH with intent to cause GBH — the most serious non-fatal offence, carrying life imprisonment

cards.front: Recall a key point about Offences Against the Person
cards.back: The key difference between s20 and s18 is the mens rea — s18 requires specific intent to cause really serious harm

cards.front: Recall a key point about Offences Against the Person
cards.back: ABH under s47 requires that assault or battery caused actual bodily harm — the harm must be more than trifling

cards.front: Recall a key point about Offences Against the Person
cards.back: A wound requires a break in both the dermis and epidermis — a scratch breaking only the outer layer is not a wound

cards.front: Recall a key point about Offences Against the Person
cards.back: GBH means really serious harm — fractures, serious internal injuries or permanent disfigurement

cards.front: Recall a key point about Offences Against the Person
cards.back: Consent can be a defence to minor offences but not to ABH or above, except in recognised exceptions (sport, surgery)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Offences Against the Person
cards.back: The Offences Against the Person Act 1861 is outdated and has been criticised for its confusing structure and language
